analysis: The relative afferent pupillary defect (RAPD) is a clinical sign indicating an asymmetry in the afferent visual pathway, typically due to damage or dysfunction. In the context of the given options: 1) Retinal detachment can lead to a loss of photoreceptor function, reducing sensory input and causing RAPD. 2) Cataracts, referred to as 'waterfall' in the options, cause lens opacity, which affects vision but does not impact the afferent pathway directly, thus not causing RAPD. 3) Optic neuritis involves inflammation of the optic nerve, impairing signal transmission and resulting in RAPD. 4) Obstruction of the central retinal vein can lead to retinal ischemia, potentially damaging photoreceptors and possibly causing RAPD. Based on standard medical knowledge, cataracts do not affect the afferent pathways directly, supporting the conclusion that cataracts do not cause RAPD. Therefore, the situation not accompanied by a relative afferent pupillary defect is cataracts.
